newsitem.title: SPAIN: Bank of Spain buying pesetas versus marks-dealers.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Spain buying pesetas versus marks-dealers.

text.p: The Bank of Spain was buying pesetas against marks in the currency market on Friday morning at around 84.85/90, dealers said.
"The central bank has been intervening all morning, buying pesetas at around 84.85/90," one dealer said.
The Bank of Spain said it does not comment on its intervention operations as a policy.
By 0955 GMT, the peseta was trading at 84.87/90 per mark after touching 84.92 per mark earlier in the session, and compared with levels seen late on Thursday of 84.77/80.
Dealers said EMU jitters were taking another swipe at Club Med currencies and worrying traders.
"There's been some talk in the market that Germany could announce an official delay for EMU's start," one dealer said.
Dealers said the central bank had also been intervening on Wednesday and last week, buying pesetas against marks at around 84.85/90, to try to keep the Spanish currency below the 85.00 level.
